label: Late-prefix / <DEL> steps in sequences starting with q/w/y/u/2, especially first m/x/z/s/3 inputs
explanation: Fires only in the original phase at t>=3 and on the <DEL> step, never at t<=2 and never during the copy phase. The <DEL> step holds about 45% of the activation mass (5.5% of DEL steps fire). The rest is original-phase steps, almost all first occurrences (in_first=1 holds 96% of the mass), with input tokens m, x, z, s, 3 (and to a lesser degree t, i, 1) heavily overrepresented. The strongest modulator is the sequence prefix: first token q gives 7x lift, and w/y/u/2 give 3-4x. Top activations are almost all sequences whose first few tokens come from {q,w,y,u,2,b,d,0}. Fires rarely when the first token is r, g, d, or e. The predicate keeps about 72% of the mass but has only about 27% precision. The unit looks like a distributed readout of hidden-state prefix composition that a token-level rule does not cleanly capture.
